text: A gentleman, knowing that I am a friend of   t h a t   o n e,   who collects materials for Bay Ganyo, handed me the letter attached here, to deliver it to him. This letter is so original and characteristic that it would not be bad to print it in the newspaper Zname as a feuilleton. How the letter fell into the hands of the gentleman — I do not know.
To the Editor of the newspaper "It's Not the Time".

Hey there, greenhorn, why have you accused me in the newspaper "It's Not the Time" of being supposedly opposition, eh? Is that all the brains you have? Does your Uncle Ganyo ever become opposition, boy? Or what did you say to yourself: let’s be fewer so we can divide more among ourselves. You’re not stupid, I know you. But you’re still stupid, to tell you the truth. That is, you’re not stupid, but you’re a bit of a novice. For these things, ask your uncle. You, so to speak, grabbed the bone yesterday, but your uncle has been gnawing on it for nine years now and has no intention of letting it go until the end of time. And you know what, boy, let me tell you the plain truth: there’s enough for you, and there’s enough for me. Long live the motherland. When I was still going to Sofia, as a delegation to beg that scoundrel not to resign, even then—remember, at the Vrazhdebna inns?—even then I realized that there’s no profit in being opposition. But, you’ll ask, why? Why indeed? Quite simple: because you’ll be left holding the broom, while the others feather their nests. And what people! A choice bunch of heroes, all educated, experienced. Our predecessors were a completely wild bunch. They stole openly, by force, amateurishly, and they even allowed themselves debaucheries, offending the honor of women, girls, and... Ah, boy, isn't it so? And finally, they fell headfirst into the trap. Look, our people today aren’t like that. As for debauchery, they’re not into it. That is—how should I put it—it’s not that they don’t do it, but who’s going to climb up Dzhendemtepe, or Nebettepe, who’s going to scour the hammams to ask what happened. And besides, whose business is it? But as for business, they’re good at it. Credit where credit is due! And they set things up so well that, shame or no shame, I’ll admit to you, brother, even I was amazed. Bravo, you rascals! Look at what a thing science is. Dealing with such people—that I understand. Our predecessors were doing things by force, they killed, they hanged, they shot, they ruined everything. And why? For nothing. But today, do you see? Only during elections they don’t let you budge, but for everything else—freedom! Shout, curse, strain yourself as much as you want—no one says a thing to you. And why would they bother the opposition—let it make its noise, who listens to it. Our people twirl their mustaches and smirk at them. The power is in their hands—they couldn’t care less. And now, when so many railways are to be built, so many companies to be forged, so many ports to be constructed, you’ve chosen exactly this time to accuse me of being supposedly opposition. Don’t do that, brother. Is that all your friendship was worth? Are you jealous of me, or what? As if you’ve hit fewer jackpots than I have. Just do the math, how many places are you getting paid from. And me—what? I’m just minding my little trade, and that’s it. And finally, you know that these things happen by agreement. If you help me get into some fat enterprise, do you really think I won’t pay you back? I know how things are done. And as if that weren't enough, you’ve gone and twisted the letter, you devil, so that when a person reads it, they’ll even think I’m against the Personage. Me? Is that how loyal a person you think I am? Didn’t we supposedly give our word that it’s not the time. I’d understand if the power weren’t in our hands, if we were sniffing from the sidelines—then, naturally, you’d see red and go after everyone, the Personage included. But now, when we’ve grabbed the bone with both hands and when it’s exactly the time to secure ourselves for our old age, should I go and say some "truthful" word about the Personage? Your Uncle Ganyo is no fool; he knows when it’s time to shout "long live!" One "long live"—hop, one enterprise. And when the time comes—we know how to shout a different tune. That’s how the world goes. If nothing else, at least we’ve understood this philosophy to the core, damn it.
Boy, did our people go too far with the Lom folk? I hear: wounded, killed! My, we’d better keep our wits about us, for... they cut off that man’s hands, lest the times turn against him...
That's enough for now. Long live His Royal Highness!

Do you see how I'm shouting "long live," yet you've gone and said that I was against it? You're jealous of me, devil take you. You know very well that if we start outshouting each other, there's no telling who will outshout whom. And if it comes to showing reverence, I won't be outdone there either. You'll kiss a hand, I—both hands; you'll kiss the hem, I—the feet; you'll kiss one place, I—an even more "other" place. Are you really trying to compete with me, you greenhorn?
